issues.legal_issue: A state agricultural-income-tax provision that disallows expenses for immature tea plants cannot be applied if doing so would produce a tea agricultural-income figure different from the figure determined under the income-tax enactments.
material_facts: A tea-estate owner incurred expenses for upkeep and maintenance of immature tea plants that yielded no agricultural income during the relevant accounting years.
The state amendment barred deductions for expenses incurred for cultivation, upkeep, or maintenance of immature plants from which no agricultural income was derived during the previous year.
The income-tax computation for the tea estate allowed the disputed expenses, while the state assessments did not.
issues.conclusion: The exclusion for expenses relating to immature plants does not apply when computing agricultural income derived from tea plantations.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(1) defines agricultural income by reference to the definition in the enactments relating to Indian income tax, and Entry 46 of List II empowers a State Legislature to tax agricultural income so defined. Under the Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, the tea-income definition adopts the income-tax treatment. Rule 24 of the Indian Income-tax Rules, 1922, read with sections 10(2)(xv) and 59 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, governs computation of income from tea grown and manufactured by the seller and the agricultural proportion of that income. The State may allow further deductions but cannot increase the agricultural income by denying an expense allowed in that computation. The court harmoniously construed Explanation 2 to section 5 of the state Act so that it did not apply to tea income; no earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: constitutional_tax_power_case and tea_income_case and immature_plant_upkeep_expense and income_tax_computation_allows_expense

predicates.constitutional_tax_power_case: The proceeding challenges the scope of a state's power to tax agricultural income.
predicates.tea_income_case: The income being computed is derived from tea grown and manufactured by the seller.
predicates.immature_plant_upkeep_expense: The taxpayer incurred upkeep or maintenance expenses for immature plants that produced no income during the accounting year.
predicates.income_tax_computation_allows_expense: The income-tax computation allows the taxpayer to deduct the disputed expense.
predicates.state_exclusion_does_not_apply_to_tea_in: The state rule excluding the expense is not applied when computing agricultural income from tea.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns state taxation of tea income and the income-tax computation allows an expense for maintaining immature plants, the state exclusion is not applied to that tea income.

issues.legal_issue: The constitutional meaning of agricultural income incorporates the applicable income-tax rules that determine the agricultural share of income derived partly from agriculture and partly from business.
material_facts: The constitutional definition of agricultural income referred to agricultural income as defined for the purposes of enactments relating to Indian income tax.
Rules made under the income-tax statute prescribed how to compute income from tea grown and manufactured by the seller and what portion was agricultural income.
Those rules were in force when the Constitution adopted the income-tax definition by reference.
issues.conclusion: The income-tax rules governing computation and apportionment form part of the definition of agricultural income incorporated by the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 366(1) refers to agricultural income as defined for the purposes of enactments relating to Indian income tax. Section 59 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, authorized rules prescribing computation and apportionment for income derived partly from agriculture and partly from business, and provided that the rules would have effect as if enacted in the Act. Rules 23 and 24 of the Indian Income-tax Rules, 1922, therefore formed part of the relevant income-tax framework incorporated by reference. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.constitutional_definition_case: The proceeding requires determination of the constitutional meaning of agricultural income.
predicates.income_tax_definition_is_incorporated: The constitutional definition refers to agricultural income as defined for income-tax purposes.
predicates.binding_computation_rules_prescribe_agri: Rules having the force of the income-tax enactment prescribe how to compute or apportion income derived from both agriculture and business.
predicates.incorporated_definition_includes_computa: The incorporated meaning of agricultural income includes the applicable income-tax computation and apportionment rules.

issues.definition: When the constitutional definition adopts the income-tax definition and binding rules prescribe agricultural apportionment, the adopted definition includes those rules.

issues.legal_issue: Expenses for upkeep and maintenance of immature tea plants already planted are running expenses rather than capital expenditure.
material_facts: The disputed expenses were for upkeep and maintenance of immature tea plants from which no agricultural income had yet been derived.
The expenses concerned plants already planted, rather than the cost of planting bushes in replacement of bushes that had died or become permanently useless.
issues.conclusion: The upkeep and maintenance expenses are running expenses and are not capital expenditure.
issues.legal_principle: In applying section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the court held that expenditure on upkeep and maintenance of immature plants is running expenditure, not capital expenditure. The proviso to Rule 24 of the Indian Income-tax Rules, 1922, concerns the cost of planting replacement bushes and does not address upkeep or maintenance of bushes already planted. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.tax_computation_case: The proceeding concerns the classification of an expense in computing taxable income.
predicates.immature_plants_already_planted: The plants had already been planted but had not yet produced income.
predicates.expense_is_for_upkeep_not_planting: The expense was for maintaining existing plants rather than planting replacement plants.
predicates.upkeep_expense_is_revenue_in_nature: The expense is treated as a running expense rather than capital expenditure.

issues.definition: When an expense concerns upkeep of already-planted immature plants rather than planting replacements, it is a running expense rather than a capital expense.
